intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic dishes like Bun Cha, Banh Mi, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Stay in a hostel within the Old Quarter itself to walk directly to food stalls upon arrival on Day 1, even with a late flight, as the night market runs until 23:00.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An during the monthly Lantern Festival, tasting White Rose Dumplings, Cao Lau noodles, and Banh Mi from street stalls. Book a guesthouse on Tran Phu Street or Nguyen Thai Hoc Street to be within a 2-minute walk of all activity hubs, maximizing every hour of your stay.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market & Backpacker Street
experiences.description: Dive into the vibrant chaos of Ben Thanh Market for fresh produce and local snacks, then head to Bui Vien Walking Street for live music, cheap beer, and grilled street food. Stay in a budget hostel on De Tham Street in District 1 to be a 5-minute walk from both hubs, making it easy to explore even after a late arrival.

experiences.name: Ninh Binh Boat Tour through Tam Coc
experiences.description: Glide through the stunning limestone karst landscape of Tam Coc on a traditional rowing boat, passing rice paddies and cave tunnels. Base yourself in Ninh Binh town center or Tam Coc village to catch early morning departures before crowds arrive, avoiding the wasted late-arrival Day 1 by pre-booking a guesthouse steps from the boat dock.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Local Com Hen Experience
experiences.description: Explore the historic Imperial Citadel and Royal Tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty, then taste Hue's signature Com Hen (clam rice) and Bun Bo Hue noodle soup from street vendors near Dong Ba Market. Stay near Dong Ba Market or the citadel area to walk to cultural sites and food stalls without transport costs, keeping the experience budget-friendly.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly 86 airport bus (45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk through the winding streets of the Old Quarter to get your bearings. Explore Hang Gai, Hang Bac, and Hang Dao streets.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake and visit the iconic Ngoc Son Temple (Jade Mountain Temple) on the island - entry around 30,000 VND. Watch locals do evening exercises around the lake. Head to the famous Bia Hoi Corner (Ta Hien Street) for a cold draft beer at just 5,000-10,000 VND per glass - a true Hanoi backpacker tradition.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi sandwich from a street vendor near the Old Quarter for 20,000-30,000 VND upon arrival
meals.dinner: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Thin or a local pho stall on Dinh Tien Hoang Street - around 50,000-70,000 VND. Follow up with fresh spring rolls from a street cart near Bia Hoi Corner.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or a local gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid taxi touts at the airport - use the official bus or a Grab app ride. Keep your belongings secure in the Old Quarter as it can be busy.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00-7:00 AM) to experience the Old Quarter morning market atmosphere. Head to Dong Xuan Market, Hanoi's largest covered market, for a peek at local commerce. Then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and Ba Dinh Square (free to view exterior, mausoleum entry is free but check opening hours - usually closed on Mondays and Fridays). Walk through the One Pillar Pagoda nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) - entry 30,000 VND - Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070. Explore its beautiful courtyards and learn about Vietnamese scholarly history. Afterward, wander through the French Quarter architecture around Hoan Kiem Lake. Visit St. Joseph's Cathedral (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Experience the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday to Sunday - if applicable). Browse local handicrafts, clothing, and souvenirs. Enjoy the vibrant street atmosphere of the Old Quarter after dark. Visit a local ca phe trung (egg coffee) cafe - a Hanoi specialty.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a street stall near Hang Ga Street - around 30,000-40,000 VND. Pair with Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da) for 15,000-25,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha (grilled pork with vermicelli noodles) - the dish made famous by Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama. Try Bun Cha Huong Lien on Le Van Huu Street for around 40,000-60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill) - a Hanoi specialty. Try a budget version at local restaurants on Cha Ca Street for 80,000-120,000 VND. Alternatively, graze on street food snacks around the Old Quarter for 50,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays, Fridays, and during October-November for maintenance. Dress modestly when visiting religious and government sites - cover shoulders and knees. Bargaining is expected at markets but do so respectfully.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Hidden Gems & Hoan Kiem)
day_by_day.morning: Start with a morning Tai Chi session by Hoan Kiem Lake (free, starts around 6:00 AM - join locals). Visit the Hanoi Museum of Ethnology (40,000 VND) - one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums showcasing Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups. The outdoor section has full-scale traditional houses from different regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Fine Arts (40,000 VND) featuring lacquerware, silk paintings, and traditional Vietnamese art. Walk back through the French Quarter admiring colonial architecture. Visit the Hoa Lo Prison Museum (30,000 VND) - the infamous 'Hanoi Hilton' with sobering history from both French colonial and Vietnam War eras.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre near Hoan Kiem Lake - tickets from 100,000 VND for a 50-minute show. This is a uniquely Vietnamese art form originating in the Red River Delta. Afterward, explore the vibrant street food scene on Ma May Street.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice) with various toppings from a street vendor near the hotel - 20,000-30,000 VND. A filling and authentic Vietnamese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) from a local restaurant near the Museum of Ethnology - 40,000-60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl around the Old Quarter: try Nem Ran (fried spring rolls), Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), and finish with a bowl of Che (sweet dessert soup) - budget 60,000-80,000 VND total for a feast.

day_by_day.notes: Book Water Puppet Show tickets in advance, especially during peak season. The Museum of Ethnology is a bit far from the Old Quarter - consider a Grab bike (xe om) for around 30,000-40,000 VND one way. April weather in Hanoi can be warm and humid with occasional drizzle - carry a small umbrella.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or train from Hanoi to Ninh Binh (about 2 hours, bus from My Dinh station costs 80,000-100,000 VND). Upon arrival, rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) or join a budget tour. Visit Tam Coc ('Three Caves') - take a sampan boat ride through stunning limestone karst scenery and rice paddies (boat ride: 150,000 VND). Often called 'Ha Long Bay on land.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry) - a beautiful temple complex built into a limestone cliff. Continue to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (20,000 VND) - Vietnam's capital in the 10th-11th centuries with ancient temples dedicated to the Dinh and Le dynasties. Climb the nearby mountain for panoramic views over the karst landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by late afternoon bus/train. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by early evening. Relax and recover from the day trip with a quiet dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street cart near the bus station before departure - 20,000-30,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (everyday rice) restaurant near Tam Coc with rice, vegetables, and grilled fish - 50,000-70,000 VND. Many simple restaurants cater to budget travelers in Ninh Binh.
meals.dinner: Return to Hanoi for a comforting bowl of Pho Ga (chicken noodle soup) at a local pho shop in the Old Quarter - 50,000-70,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Start very early (6:00-7:00 AM) to make the most of the day trip. The boat ride at Tam Coc involves rowing women who may push souvenir sales - politely decline if not interested. Beware of overpriced tourist restaurants near major attractions in Ninh Binh - walk a few minutes away for local prices. Total day trip budget: approximately 400,000-500,000 VND including transport.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hanoi accommodation. Take a budget overnight train or early morning train to Hue (The Reunification Express - Train SE3 or SE5 departs around 6:00-9:00 AM, hard seat from 200,000 VND, soft seat from 300,000 VND, sleeper from 400,000 VND). The journey takes approximately 12-14 hours but offers stunning scenery through mountains and coastal views. Alternatively, take a budget airline (Vietjet/Bamboo) for 300,000-600,000 VND if booked in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: If traveling by train, enjoy the scenic journey through the Hai Van Pass area - one of Vietnam's most dramatic rail routes hugging coastal cliffs. Bring snacks and enjoy the passing Vietnamese countryside. If flying, arrive in Hue by early afternoon and check into a budget guesthouse in the city center (dorms from 100,000 VND, private rooms from 200,000-300,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue and check into accommodation near Pham Ngu Lao Street or near the Citadel area. Take a gentle evening walk along the Perfume River. Explore the local Dong Ba Market area for evening street food.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure at a local com pho shop near your Hanoi hotel - 40,000-60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Train food or packed lunch of Banh Mi and snacks bought before boarding - 30,000-50,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) - the city's signature dish and arguably Vietnam's most flavorful noodle soup. Find it at a local street stall for 40,000-60,000 VND. This is a must-try upon arrival in Hue.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance through Vietnam Railways website or a travel agent in Hanoi (small booking fee applies). The overnight sleeper train is a classic backpacker experience and saves on accommodation costs. Store valuables securely on overnight trains. If flying, factor in airport transfer costs (Hue airport is about 15km from city center - taxi around 150,000-200,000 VND or local bus for much less).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (150,000 VND) - the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors. Explore the massive walled complex including the Forbidden Purple City, Thai Hoa Palace, and various pavilions. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Vietnam's most important historical monuments. Spend 2-3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) or hire a xe om to visit the Royal Tombs along the Perfume River. The Tomb of Minh Mang (100,000 VND) and Tomb of Tu Duc (100,000 VND) are the most impressive - ornate complexes set in forested grounds. Alternatively, take a budget dragon boat cruise on the Perfume River (negotiate for 100,000-150,000 VND per person) to visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free entry) - Hue's iconic seven-story tower.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dong Ba Market - Hue's largest traditional market - for local produce, spices, and crafts. Walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Explore the backpacker street area for evening entertainment and cheap drinks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake) from a street stall - 30,000-50,000 VND. A local specialty not to be missed.
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) or Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) at a local restaurant near the Citadel - 30,000-50,000 VND. Hue is famous for its unique royal cuisine.
meals.dinner: Visit a local com binh dan restaurant for a full set meal with rice, multiple dishes, and soup for 50,000-80,000 VND. Try Hue-style vegetarian food if curious - the city has a strong Buddhist culinary tradition.

day_by_day.notes: A combo ticket for multiple Hue monuments is available and saves money if visiting several sites. The Citadel is large - wear comfortable shoes. Hue's cuisine is distinctly different from Hanoi - it tends to be spicier and more complex. The city has a more relaxed pace than Hanoi - enjoy it. April can bring rain in Hue - carry an umbrella.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (Travel to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hue accommodation. Take a budget bus or join a shared minivan transfer to Hoi An (approximately 3-4 hours, cost 150,000-200,000 VND). The route crosses the spectacular Hai Van Pass - ask to stop for photos at the top if taking a private or shared transfer. Alternatively, rent a motorbike for the scenic coastal drive if you have riding experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check into a budget guesthouse or hostel (dorms from 100,000 VND, private rooms from 200,000-350,000 VND) in the An Bang Beach area or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on foot - the beautifully preserved trading port with Japanese, Chinese, and European architectural influences. Buy a combined entrance ticket (120,000 VND) to access the heritage sites.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical Hoi An Ancient Town at night when lanterns illuminate the streets and Thu Bon River. Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge (included in ticket). Browse the colorful lantern shops. Watch the river lantern ceremony if timing aligns. The town transforms beautifully after dark.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Hue - a final bowl of Bun Bo Hue or Banh Mi for 30,000-50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish) at a local restaurant in Hoi An's Ancient Town - 50,000-80,000 VND. These dishes are unique to Hoi An.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong - arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi shop (featured by Anthony Bourdain) on Phan Chau Trinh Street - just 25,000-35,000 VND for a legendary sandwich. Supplement with fresh fruit from street vendors.

day_by_day.notes: Cao Lau noodles are unique to Hoi An - the dish uses water from a specific local well and local ash lye. Hoi An is very popular with tourists so prices are slightly higher than other cities - seek out local restaurants away from the main tourist strip. The Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Many tailors offer cheap custom clothing - allow 2-3 days for alterations if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach (about 3km from the Ancient Town) for a relaxing morning. The beach is less crowded than Cua Dai and has a more local feel. Swim, relax, and enjoy the coastline. Some beach bars offer free sun loungers with a drink purchase.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Ancient Town and visit the Assembly Halls (Chinese congregational halls) - Fujian Assembly Hall and Cantonese Assembly Hall are highlights (included in Ancient Town ticket). Take a cooking class if budget allows (some classes start from 300,000-400,000 VND and include a market visit). Alternatively, visit the Hoi An Museum of History and Culture (free with Ancient Town ticket) and the Museum of Folk Culture.
day_by_day.evening: Join a lantern-making workshop (100,000-150,000 VND) - a fun hands-on cultural activity. Release a paper lantern on the Thu Bon River (20,000-30,000 VND). Explore the riverside night market for local crafts and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (Hoi An-style turmeric noodles with pork, shrimp, and peanuts) from a local pho shop - 40,000-60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at An Bang Beach - grilled fish or prawns from a local beach shack for 80,000-150,000 VND. Freshly grilled with local spices.
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An-style chicken rice) - a beloved local dish available at many small restaurants on Phan Chu Trinh Street for 40,000-60,000 VND. Simple, delicious, and authentically local.

day_by_day.notes: Full Moon Festival (Hoi An Lantern Festival) occurs on the 14th of each lunar month - if your dates align, this is a spectacular event when the Ancient Town turns off electric lights and is illuminated entirely by lanterns. Check the lunar calendar. An Bang Beach has some beach bars with happy hours - great for budget socializing with other backpackers. Stay hydrated in the April heat.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hoi An accommodation. Transfer to Da Nang Airport (30 minutes by taxi/Grab - around 150,000-200,000 VND). Take a budget domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) - book in advance with Vietjet or Bamboo Airways for 300,000-700,000 VND. Flight duration is approximately 1.5 hours. Alternatively, take an overnight bus (sleeper bus from 200,000-300,000 VND, 18+ hours) to save on accommodation costs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). Take a Grab or airport bus (109 bus - 20,000 VND) to the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district in District 1. Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse (dorms from 100,000 VND, private rooms from 200,000-350,000 VND). Get oriented in the buzzing backpacker hub. Visit nearby Ben Thanh Market for a first taste of Saigon's energy.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pham Ngu Lao area - the legendary Southeast Asian backpacker hub. Walk to the nearby Bui Vien Walking Street (open from evening) - the famous party street lined with bars, street food, and neon lights. Experience the chaotic, exciting energy of Saigon nightlife. Grab a cheap bia hoi and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Hoi An - a final Banh Mi Phuong or bowl of Mi Quang for 30,000-50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks if flying, or pack food for the bus journey. Budget 50,000-80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork chop, egg, and pickled vegetables) - the quintessential Saigon street food dish. Find it at any local com tam stall near Pham Ngu Lao for 50,000-80,000 VND. A must-eat in HCMC.

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is legendary - crossing the street requires confidence (walk slowly and steadily, traffic flows around you). Grab app is essential for safe and fairly priced transport in the city. Be aware of motorbike bag snatching in tourist areas - keep bags on the side away from the road. The city is officially Ho Chi Minh City but locals still commonly call it Saigon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (40,000 VND) - a powerful and sobering museum documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Graphic but essential for understanding modern Vietnamese history. Nearby, visit the Reunification Palace (40,000 VND) - the former South Vietnamese presidential palace where the war ended on April 30, 1975, with the famous tank crashing through the gates. Both sites are within walking distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (free exterior viewing) and the historic Saigon Central Post Office - a stunning French colonial building still in operation. Walk through the French Quarter architecture of District 1. Visit Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee Hall. Browse the Ben Thanh Market area for last-minute souvenirs (bargain hard - initial prices are often 3-5x the fair price).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam - splurge slightly on a rooftop bar for sunset views over the Saigon skyline (many have happy hours with 2-for-1 cocktails from 5:00-7:00 PM). Return to the street food scene for a final Vietnamese feast. Reflect on the incredible journey through Vietnam's diverse landscapes, history, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near the hostel - 25,000-35,000 VND. Saigon-style Banh Mi is slightly different from Hanoi - often with more fillings and a sweeter bread.
meals.lunch: Hu Tieu (Southern-style clear noodle soup with pork and seafood) from a local restaurant near the War Remnants Museum - 40,000-60,000 VND. A distinctly Southern Vietnamese dish.
meals.dinner: Final Vietnamese feast: Lau (Vietnamese hotpot) shared with fellow travelers at a local restaurant near Pham Ngu Lao - 100,000-150,000 VND per person including fresh vegetables, meat, and seafood. Toast to an incredible Vietnam adventure with a final ca phe sua da.

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum contains very graphic imagery - be mentally prepared. If departing from Tan Son Nhat Airport, allow extra time for Saigon traffic (at least 1.5-2 hours before your flight). Keep some VND for airport snacks but exchange remaining dong back to USD before leaving as VND is non-convertible outside Vietnam. Consider a day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (budget tours from 150,000-200,000 VND) if you have extra time before departure - a fascinating underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong fighters.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or airport bus (Bus 86) to the Old Quarter hotel (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle stroll around the Old Quarter to shake off travel fatigue. Walk the 36 ancient guild streets (Hang Gai, Hang Bac, Hang Ma). Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and photograph Ngoc Son Temple on the Huc Bridge from the lakeside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun; if a weekday, wander Ta Hien Beer Street instead). Soak in the buzzing street atmosphere, grab a cold Bia Hoi (draught beer, ~20 cents a glass) and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street cart near the Old Quarter after check-in (~30,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha Huong Lien (famous spot on Le Van Huu St) — grilled pork with rice noodles, ~80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Exchange currency at the airport or a local bank (avoid hotel rates). Grab a local SIM card at the airport for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex early (opens 7:30 AM) — see the Presidential Palace, One Pillar Pagoda, and Ho Chi Minh Museum. Book tickets in advance; dress modestly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first university built in 1070. Spend time in the tranquil courtyards. Afterward, visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry) for a deep dive into the country's 54 ethnic groups.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter. Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Book tickets same-day at the box office.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — iconic Hanoi-style, ~60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Thang (delicate Hanoi noodle soup) at a local eatery near the Ethnology Museum, ~70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — turmeric grilled fish with dill, a Hanoi specialty, ~150,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and for maintenance periods. Check the official schedule before visiting. Wear long pants and covered shoulders.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (~2 hrs by bus or booked minivan). Head to Trang An Landscape Complex — take a 2-hour rowing boat tour through limestone karsts, caves, and rice paddies. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or rent a motorbike (~80,000 VND/day) to Mua Cave. Climb ~500 steps to the summit for a panoramic view over Tam Coc valley — one of the most photogenic spots in northern Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by early evening. Wind down with a walk along Hoan Kiem Lake after dark when it is beautifully lit. Stop for egg coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Giang — a Hanoi invention.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street vendor near the hotel, ~30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or fresh spring rolls at a local restaurant in Ninh Binh town, ~80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at Banh Cuon Gia Truyen in the Old Quarter, ~60,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared minivan transfer to Ninh Binh through your hotel or a travel agency (~150,000–200,000 VND each way). Start early (7:00 AM) to beat the crowds at Trang An.

day_by_day.morning: Overnight sleeper train or early morning flight to Hue (book 2-3 days ahead). The train ride (~14 hrs) is scenic and budget-friendly; opt for a soft-sleeper berth (~400,000–600,000 VND). If flying, the journey is ~1 hr (~800,000–1,200,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hue. Check into a mid-range guesthouse near the Perfume River. After settling in, visit the Imperial Citadel (Dai Noi) — the walled royal city of the Nguyen Dynasty. Explore the Forbidden Purple City ruins and the Thai Hoa Palace (~150,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Explore Dong Ba Market for local crafts and snacks. Enjoy Hue's famous street food scene.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or instant noodles on the train / airport snack
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Phuong or a local com binh dan (everyday Vietnamese set meal) near the station, ~60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup — the dish originates here) at a local restaurant near Dong Ba Market, ~70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: If taking the sleeper train from Hanoi, depart the evening of Day 3 and arrive Day 4 morning — adjust accordingly. Flying is faster but less atmospheric for backpackers.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike and explore the Royal Tombs south of Hue. Visit Tomb of Tu Duc (most picturesque) and Tomb of Khai Dinh (dramatic hilltop fusion architecture). Each tomb costs ~150,000 VND entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's iconic 7-tiered tower on the Perfume River. Take a short dragon boat cruise back along the river (~100,000 VND). Browse the local craft villages of Phu Cam for conical hat (Non La) making.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Hue Royal Court Music (Nha Nhac) dinner cruise on the Perfume River — a UNESCO-recognized musical tradition (~200,000–300,000 VND including dinner). Book through guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style sizzling crispy pancake) at a local stall, ~50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) — a Hue street food specialty on Con Hen islet, ~40,000 VND
meals.dinner: Included in the dinner cruise, or dine at Lac Thien Restaurant (famous family-run spot) for a Hue set meal, ~120,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Hue can be very hot in April. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. A combo ticket for multiple royal tombs is available and saves money (~360,000 VND for 5 sites).

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Hue to Hoi An via the Hai Van Pass — one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads. Take a booked motorbike tour or private car (~300,000–500,000 VND). Stop at the summit viewpoint and Lang Co Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An. Check into a mid-range homestay or boutique guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky Old House, and Phung Hung Old House (~120,000 VND combo ticket).
day_by_day.evening: The Ancient Town glows with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns at night — the best time to explore. Walk the lantern-lit streets, shop for custom tailoring, and soak up the atmosphere along the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart before departure, ~30,000 VND
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Cao Lau noodles at White Rose Restaurant — dishes unique to Hoi An, ~100,000 VND
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at Ba Buoi Restaurant — a local institution, ~80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass road transfer is highly recommended for the scenery. Alternatively, the Da Nang–Hoi An route by bus is cheaper (~50,000 VND) if you prefer. Hoi An Ancient Town entry tickets are required after 5 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from the Ancient Town). Enjoy a relaxed morning swim and beach time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day Vietnamese cooking class (~400,000–600,000 VND) — most include a guided market visit to Hoi An Central Market, followed by hands-on cooking of 3–4 traditional dishes. A highlight for food lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Browse the tailors on Tran Phu and Le Loi Streets if interested in custom-made clothing (allow 24–48 hrs for tailoring). Enjoy a sunset drink at a riverside cafe. Explore the night market on Nguyen Hoang Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi shop, ~35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at a riverside restaurant — grilled prawns, squid, and clams, ~150,000–200,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class a day in advance. Hoi An is very walkable and bikeable — no need for motorbikes within town. Stay hydrated; April can be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early flight or overnight sleeper bus from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC / Saigon) — flight is ~1 hr (~800,000–1,500,000 VND). Arrive and check into a mid-range hotel in District 1 (Bui Vien backpacker area or Ben Thanh area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into HCMC history: visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering look at the Vietnam War. Then walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ben Thanh Street Food Market (indoor/outdoor market near Ben Thanh roundabout) — dozens of stalls serving every Vietnamese dish imaginable. Wander Bui Vien Walking Street for the famous backpacker nightlife atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Airport snack or grab Banh Mi near Da Nang airport
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa — HCMC's most celebrated Banh Mi, loaded with fillings, ~45,000 VND
meals.dinner: Ben Thanh Street Food Market — try multiple dishes: Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), and Che dessert, ~150,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is intense — use Grab (ride-hailing app) for safe and affordable transport. Download the app before arriving. Keep valuables secure in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest of HCMC). Book a half-day guided tour (~300,000–500,000 VND including transport) — crawl through the wartime tunnel network, see booby traps, and learn about Viet Cong guerrilla warfare. A fascinating and unique experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) — a stunning Taoist temple with intricate carvings and incense smoke. Explore the colorful Chinatown district of Cho Lon — visit Binh Tay Market and Thien Hau Temple.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the rooftop of the Bitexco Financial Tower for panoramic city views at sunset (~200,000 VND). Afterward, explore the upscale Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the HCMC City Hall at night.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) at a local District 1 eatery, ~70,000 VND
meals.lunch: Banh Mi or Com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) near Cu Chi before return, ~60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Com Tam Bui Saigon — iconic broken rice restaurant, ~90,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cu Chi Tunnels tour through your hotel or a reputable agency (Sinh Tourist, etc.). The Ben Duoc site is less crowded than Ben Dinh — ask for it specifically.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Vietnam — visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon (exterior only, under restoration) and the Central Post Office (a beautiful French colonial building, still functioning). Browse the surrounding streets for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last lunch in Saigon. Visit the Ho Chi Minh City Museum (~30,000 VND) for a final overview of the city's layered history. If time allows, stroll through Tao Dan Park — a peaceful green escape in the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure. Allow 2–3 hours before your flight. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Vietnam's north, center, and south.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls with pork and mushrooms) at a local cafe, ~60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Pho 2000 near Ben Thanh Market (historic spot where Bill Clinton dined) — Pho Bo, ~90,000 VND
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a final Banh Mi for the road

day_by_day.notes: Pack light souvenirs: Vietnamese coffee (Trung Nguyen), silk items, lacquerware, and Pho spice kits make great gifts. Declare any food items when going through customs. Keep one USD 25 for airport taxi if needed.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi (approximately 45 minutes). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the vibrant alleyways. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake — a serene introduction to Hanoi's spiritual heart. Browse premium silk and lacquerware boutiques nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the pedestrianized Hoan Kiem Lake promenade as the city lights up. Enjoy the buzzing atmosphere of the Old Quarter Night Market on Hang Dao Street. Wind down with a signature cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or nearby: Pho cuon (fresh rice paper rolls) and iced Vietnamese coffee at Quan An Ngon, a premium open-air Vietnamese restaurant on Phan Dinh Phung Street.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Verticale by Didier Corlou — a celebrated fine-dining restaurant in a French colonial villa blending Vietnamese spices with French technique. Signature dishes include five-spice duck and Vietnamese herb-infused amuse-bouches.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins post-arrival. Keep the pace relaxed to recover from the flight. Ensure your hotel arranges a private airport transfer in advance. April in Hanoi is warm (26–32°C) with occasional brief showers — carry a light umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural tour of the Ba Dinh Historical Quarter. Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum (exterior viewing and surrounding gardens), the Presidential Palace grounds, and the iconic One Pillar Pagoda. Continue to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070. Hire a private English-speaking historian guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology — one of Southeast Asia's finest ethnographic museums, showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam through immersive exhibits and outdoor reconstructed village structures. Followed by a leisurely cyclo (pedicab) ride back through the French Quarter, admiring colonial architecture along Trang Tien and Ngo Quyen streets.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre — a UNESCO-recognized art form originating in the Red River Delta. Book premium front-row seats in advance. Post-show, explore the vibrant Ta Hien Beer Street for authentic street food snacking.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Cafe Pho Co — a hidden gem accessed through a silk shop on Hang Gai Street, offering traditional Vietnamese breakfast (banh mi, xoi, and Vietnamese drip coffee) with stunning views over Hoan Kiem Lake.
meals.lunch: Bun cha (grilled pork with vermicelli noodles) at Bun Cha Huong Lien — the legendary restaurant made famous by Anthony Bourdain and President Obama. A quintessential Hanoi street food experience elevated by its cultural significance.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca La Vong — Hanoi's most iconic restaurant, serving the city's signature dish: cha ca (turmeric-marinated snakehead fish grilled tableside with dill and spring onions). A 150-year-old institution.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and is only open in the mornings (7:30–10:30 AM). Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for all temple and mausoleum visits. Book Water Puppet Theatre tickets at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Ninh Binh (approximately 2 hours by private car). Begin with a scenic bamboo boat ride through the Trang An Landscape Complex — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Glide through limestone karst caves, rice paddies, and ancient temples along the Ngo Dong River. This is often described as 'Halong Bay on land.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb the 500 steps to the summit of Hang Mua Peak for panoramic views over the Tam Coc valley and karst mountains — one of Vietnam's most breathtaking viewpoints. Afterward, visit Bich Dong Pagoda, a 15th-century cave pagoda built into a limestone cliff. Return to Hanoi by private car in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in the Old Quarter. Join a premium street food walking tour led by a local culinary expert — sample banh mi, nem ran (fried spring rolls), banh cuon (steamed rice rolls), and che (sweet dessert soups) from carefully vetted street vendors across the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure. Traditional Vietnamese pho bo (beef noodle soup) — the quintessential Hanoi morning meal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant in Ninh Binh: fresh goat meat (de nui) — the local specialty of the region — served with rice wine and pickled vegetables at Van Long Eco-Tourism Area restaurant.
meals.dinner: Street food tour doubles as dinner. Conclude the evening with a nightcap at Polite Pub or Summit Lounge rooftop bar in the Old Quarter.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (7:00–7:30 AM) to make the most of Ninh Binh before midday heat. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Hang Mua climb. Bring sunscreen and a hat. The premium street food tour can be booked through operators like Hanoi Street Food Tours or Devour Hanoi.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight or private transfer to Hoi An (via Da Nang Airport — approximately 1.5-hour flight). Check into a luxury boutique hotel in or near Hoi An Ancient Town (upgrade recommendation: Anantara Hoi An Resort or The Nam Hai). Freshen up and take a first walk through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural tour of Hoi An Ancient Town. Visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, Tan Ky Old House (a 200-year-old merchant's home), and the vibrant Central Market. Explore the tailoring district — Hoi An is renowned for bespoke custom clothing made within 24–48 hours. Commission a premium ao dai (traditional Vietnamese dress) or tailored suit.
day_by_day.evening: As lantern lights illuminate the Thu Bon River at dusk, join a private lantern boat ride along the river — a magical and iconic Hoi An experience. Release a flower lantern onto the river for good luck. Afterward, explore the Ancient Town by foot as it transforms into a glowing lantern wonderland.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hoi An hotel upon arrival (or airport lounge if departing early from Hanoi).
meals.lunch: Cao lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and crispy rice crackers) at Thanh Cao Lau — an authentic local restaurant in the Ancient Town. This dish is unique to Hoi An, traditionally made with water from a specific ancient Cham well.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Market Restaurant by Morning Glory — owned by celebrated local chef Trinh Diem Vy, offering a refined take on Hoi An street food classics in an elegant setting. Try white rose dumplings (banh bao vac) and fried wontons.

day_by_day.notes: Book the lantern boat ride through your hotel concierge for a private experience. If visiting on the 14th of the lunar month, the Full Moon Lantern Festival transforms the town — electricity is switched off and the streets glow entirely by candlelight and lanterns. Hoi An is compact and best explored on foot or by bicycle.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class at Red Bridge Cooking School — set on a picturesque island on the Thu Bon River, accessible by boat. Learn to prepare authentic Hoi An dishes including white rose dumplings, cao lau, and fresh spring rolls under the guidance of expert local chefs. The class includes a market tour and herb garden visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon excursion to My Son Sanctuary — a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the ruins of the ancient Cham civilization, set dramatically in a jungle valley surrounded by mountains. Hire a private guide to bring the 4th–14th century Hindu temple complex to life. Return to Hoi An by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of your hotel or at Cargo Club Restaurant overlooking the Ancient Town and river. Stroll through the lantern-lit streets of the Ancient Town and browse premium silk lantern and lacquerware shops for souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Try banh mi Hoi An — the local version of Vietnam's iconic sandwich, considered among the best in the country. Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street is legendary.
meals.lunch: Lunch is included as part of the Red Bridge cooking class — you eat what you cook.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Mango Restaurant — a sophisticated riverside restaurant with a creative menu blending Vietnamese and international flavors. Elegant ambiance with views over the Thu Bon River.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM — book in advance as spots fill quickly. My Son is best visited in the late afternoon to avoid peak heat and tour groups. Wear comfortable shoes and insect repellent for the jungle ruins.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise bicycle ride through the countryside surrounding Hoi An — pedal through emerald rice paddies, water buffalo fields, and traditional fishing villages along the Thu Bon River delta. Visit Tra Que Vegetable Village, an organic farming community that supplies herbs to Hoi An's restaurants. Participate in a brief farming experience with local families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach — pristine stretches of coastline just 5 km from the Ancient Town. Relax at a premium beach club (Naman Retreat Beach Club recommended) with sun loungers, fresh coconuts, and beachside service. Optional: kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — approximately 1.5-hour flight. Evening arrival and private luxury transfer to hotel in District 1 (recommendation: Park Hyatt Saigon or Reverie Saigon — one of Asia's most opulent hotels).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cycling tour. Fresh fruit, yogurt, and Vietnamese iced coffee at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant at An Bang Beach — grilled prawns, steamed clams with lemongrass, and fresh fish. Simple, fresh, and exceptional quality.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Saigon at Cuc Gach Quan — a beloved restaurant set in a beautifully restored French colonial house, serving rustic Vietnamese home-cooking elevated to an art form. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City flight in advance. An Bang Beach has excellent beachside dining options. Tra Que Village cycling tour can be arranged through your hotel or local operators — typically a 3-hour morning experience.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive cultural morning in Ho Chi Minh City's District 1. Begin at the War Remnants Museum — one of the most powerful and thought-provoking museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam-American War with striking photography and artifacts. Follow with a visit to the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) — preserved exactly as it was on April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French colonial architectural heritage of Saigon: the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (exterior — under renovation), the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the Opera House. Then head to Ben Thanh Market for a premium street food tasting circuit — sample banh xeo (sizzling crepes), goi cuon (fresh spring rolls), and fresh sugarcane juice.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop sundowners at Saigon Saigon Bar at the historic Caravelle Hotel — a legendary Saigon institution where war correspondents once gathered. Afterward, explore the vibrant Bui Vien Walking Street for a taste of Saigon's electric nightlife energy, then retreat to a sophisticated cocktail bar like The Reverie's Lobby Lounge.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the hotel (Park Hyatt or Reverie offers exceptional breakfast spreads with Vietnamese and international options).
meals.lunch: Banh mi and street snacks at Ben Thanh Market area, followed by a bowl of hu tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) — a Saigon specialty — at a local stall on Vo Van Tan Street.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark — a unique Saigon dining experience where guests eat in complete darkness served by visually impaired staff. The menu features refined Vietnamese cuisine. A genuinely transformative and memorable luxury experience.

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum can be emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Dress modestly for the Reunification Palace. Book Noir. Dining in the Dark well in advance as it is extremely popular. Bui Vien Street is best after 9 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (approximately 1.5 hours northwest of Saigon). Opt for the Ben Duoc site over the more touristy Ben Dinh — it is quieter, more atmospheric, and set within a memorial forest. With a private guide, crawl through the expanded tunnel sections, examine original trap mechanisms, and gain deep historical insight into the Viet Cong's extraordinary underground network.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Cao Dai Holy See in Tay Ninh — the ornate, psychedelic temple of the Cao Dai religion, one of Vietnam's most visually stunning and unique spiritual sites. Witness the midday prayer ceremony (12:00 PM) conducted by white-robed worshippers in a cathedral that blends Buddhist, Taoist, Confucian, and Catholic elements.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saigon. Relaxed evening in the Dong Khoi area — browse premium Vietnamese art galleries (Craig Thomas Gallery recommended), and enjoy a leisurely dinner in the city's most elegant dining precinct.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Cu Chi or Tay Ninh — fresh Vietnamese countryside cooking at a local restaurant. Try canh chua (sour tamarind fish soup) and ca kho to (caramelized fish in clay pot) — quintessential southern Vietnamese flavors.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Anan Saigon — Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's acclaimed restaurant in Cho Lon (Chinatown), reimagining Vietnamese street food with fine-dining precision. The pho foie gras and banh mi wagyu are legendary. One of Asia's most exciting restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:30 AM to reach Cu Chi before the heat peaks. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dusty in the tunnels. The Cao Dai ceremony is free to observe but maintain respectful silence and photograph from the balcony only. Anan Saigon requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat day trip to the Mekong Delta — departing from Saigon to My Tho or Ben Tre (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Board a traditional wooden sampan and navigate narrow waterways through dense coconut palm forests, past floating markets, and alongside river communities. Visit a coconut candy workshop, a honey bee farm, and a traditional rice paper factory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch on a private river island, then continue deeper into the delta to experience the extraordinary floating market culture. Visit Cai Be Floating Market — vendors selling tropical fruits, vegetables, and goods from wooden boats. Explore the French colonial merchant's house of Vinh Long province. Return to Saigon by private speedboat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Saigon. Splurge on a premium farewell dinner, then take a nighttime Saigon River cruise aboard a private or semi-private vessel — watching the glittering skyline of District 1 and the Bitexco Financial Tower from the water.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before early departure.
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta feast on a river island: elephant ear fish (ca tai tuong) served whole and crispy, fresh spring rolls wrapped in rice paper with river herbs, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Deck Saigon — an elegant riverside restaurant in District 2 with stunning Saigon River views, serving contemporary Vietnamese cuisine with premium ingredients. Perfect sundowner and dinner setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Mekong Delta private tour through your hotel concierge for a tailored, crowd-free experience. Bring sunscreen and a hat — the delta is exposed and sunny. The Saigon River cruise can be arranged through Les Rives Experience or similar premium operators.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Ho Chi Minh City. Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Visit the Binh Tay Market in Cho Lon (Chinatown) — a more authentic and less touristy alternative to Ben Thanh, offering a fascinating glimpse into Saigon's Chinese-Vietnamese community and wholesale trade culture. Browse for premium Vietnamese coffee, dried spices, and artisan goods as final souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute tailored souvenir shopping along Dong Khoi Street and in the premium boutiques of the Vincom Center. Visit the Fine Arts Museum of Ho Chi Minh City — housed in a stunning French colonial building, showcasing Vietnamese art from the 20th century to present day. Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City. Relax in the premium airport lounge before your flight, reflecting on 10 extraordinary days across Vietnam's most iconic cities and landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the hotel — Vietnamese egg coffee (ca phe trung), fresh tropical fruit platter, and banh mi with premium charcuterie.
meals.lunch: Final Vietnamese lunch at Nha Hang Ngon (260 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia) — a beloved open-air restaurant serving dishes from all regions of Vietnam in a beautiful colonial courtyard. A perfect culinary farewell to the country.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or light meal before the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and security. The premium airport lounge at Tan Son Nhat (Lotus Lounge or Vietnam Airlines Business Lounge) offers comfortable seating, showers, and dining. Consider purchasing Vietnamese Trung Nguyen Legend premium coffee and Marou single-origin chocolate as high-quality take-home gifts.
